newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds inland waterway vessel scrapping programme.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds inland waterway vessel scrapping programme.

text.p: The European Court of Justice upheld on Thursday the inland waterway transport regulation, rejecting claims by shipping concerns that the regulation's aim of reducing overcapacity in waterways infringes basic rights.

The regulation introduced a scrapping scheme, to be financed by the shipping industry, as part of its basic aim to substantially reduce the number of cargo vessels and pusher craft currently on the inland waterway in the Community.

Two ship operators in Germany, required under the regulation to contribute to the scrapping fund, challenged the regulation as violating fundamental rights, based on unsubstantiated concerns and not appropriate.
The court rejected those arguments and found the vessel owners' contribution to the scrapping fund did not significantly add to their operating costs or impair their competitive position.
Reference for a preliminary ruling by the Oberverwaltungsgericht fur das Land nordrhein-Westfalen (Germany) in the proceedings pending before that court between

on the validity of Council regulation (EEC) No 1101/89 on structural improvements in inland waterway transport (OJ 1989 L 116, p. 25), and of Commission regulation (EEC) No 1102/89 laying down certain measures for implementing regulation no 1101/89, as amended by Commission regulation (EEC) No 3685/89 (OJ 1989 L 360, p. 20)

Examination of the questions referred has revealed no factor of such a kind as to affect the validity of Council regulation (EEC) No 1101/89 on structural improvements in inland waterway transport, and of Commission regulation (EEC) No 1102/89 laying down certain measures for implementing regulation no 1101/89, as amended by Commission regulation (EEC) No 3685/89.
